recipes.name: Slow Cooker Chicken Mole
ingredients_raw: 1 finely chopped canned chipotle chile in adobo sauce

steps.text: Place onion, raisins, garlic, sesame seeds, chopped chipotle pepper, peanut butter, and crushed tomatoes in slow cooker. Stir in sugar, cinnamon, chili powder, cumin, coriander, nutmeg, and cocoa powder. Place chicken in the sauce.
Cover; cook on Low until chicken is very tender, about 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Chicken Mole
raw_recipe.description: A unique blend of spices and cocoa powder turns into a rich and complex mole sauce after a long simmer in the slow cooker. Along with the tender chicken, it's a great filler for soft tortillas, or as a dip with corn chips.

review.reviewBody: I've noticed a few comments that it is too 'hot".... please read the recipe... it calls for ONE - finely chopped canned chipotle...... NOT one entire can of them! LOL.... thanks for the giggle! If you follow the recipe you will end up with a very nice mole!

This is a perfect mole sauce that is so easy! I added one small can of stewed tomatoes because I wanted more sauce, and since I didn't have corriander I used cilantro. Next time I will omit the sugar because the rasins and peanut butter add enough sweetness. Half of an adobe chipotle will add the heat to please tender palettes. I never thought I would make a homemade mole sauce but this was very easy!

I absolutely love mole but am also VERY picky about the quality. This was the closest thing to authentic mole that I have been able to find! Delicious! 
I added 2 circles of mexican chocolate though in place of the other chocolate it calls for and I added some extra peanut butter. This was so easy and tastes FANTASTIC! I had leftover mole for a couple of days and it was still great!

this was so delicious i could not believe i made this !!
i followed the recepipe to a T however i diced up 2 chipotle peppers & used 1 whole "abuelita" chocolate disk (mexican hot chocolate found in the ethnic aisle of youre local grocer)..
ps , if youre debating the peanut butter part, dont hesitate.. my mexican grandmother also used p.b in her mole..
i actually used chicken boneless thighs ( breasts dry out )& threw in 2 drumsticks & the meat fell off the bone sparkling clean...
i served this w/frijoles, white rice & avocado & cilantro garnish....
i will use this recipe forever!

I was so surprised at the tastiness and simplicity of this mole. It really is comparable to other chicken mole dishes that I have enjoyed at authentic mexican restaurants. It was so easy too! We don't have canned chipotle's here, so I added in a fresh jalapeno and some chipotle seasoning and it worked out perfectly. Served with brown rice, plain yogurt (sub for sour cream) and fresh cilantro. Highly recommend this one! We will definitely make again! Thank you!

Very tasty! Something to consider is that there is no salt in this recipe other than what's contributed by the canned tomatoes, peanut butter, and chipotles. I used natural peanut butter (as in, one ingredient - peanuts) and low-sodium tomatoes, so added some salt at the end too. Also, it seemed slightly bitter (probably due to the lack of added sugar in the natural peanut butter), so I stirred in about a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar, which instantly solved the problem. Will definitely be making this one again!

Very good! You could spend all day in the kitchen roasting and grinding peppers and spices, simmering, stewing and blending or you could take a few minutes to put these ingredients in the crock pot and get results almost as good.

I made only one change - I had some Mexican chocolate and tossed that in rather than the unsweetened cocoa and sugar. I doubt it really changed the taste.

This is a keeper.

eta: (1) I made this later using cocoa powder instead of Mexican chocolate and, although it was good, it was better with the Mexican chocolate. (2) Don't skip the raisins, they add depth to the flavor. (3) I do prefer to blend it with a hand blender to get a smooth sauce. This also helps if you don't like the texture of the raisins. (4) This is a lot of sauce for the meat. I prefer to cook and add the meat separately - otherwise too much of this yummy sauce would go to waste. (5) Finally, there is a lot of variation in chili powders and different ones will give different results. They are a mix of chilies and spices. The right chili powder makes a lot of difference. The last time I made this I had a local chili powder I purchased in Hatch, New Mexico and this was the best yet.

Meets ALL criteria!
This was super easy, very filling, economical, and not a calorie-blow. It is one that I will go back to again and again.

One thing I will do differently: saute the onions before putting in the slow cooker. They seemed a little undercooked. Otherwise, it was great!

This was really tasty! I love mole sauce when we go out for Mexican food. This recipe was just as good as what I order. I shredded the chicken and served it with sour cream and tortilla chips. Delicious! 
NOTE: Dont skip the raisins, they plumped up and gave a nice sweet balance to the spice of the sauce. 
NOTE 2: Dont use the entire car of chipotle chilis. The recipe calls for one and that was enough to give a nice kick but it was not too spicy.

I made this recipe "as is" the first time and it was good. I have made it many more times but have tweaked it since. I would say it is now "very good". I use 1TBSP brown sugar instead of white sugar. It needs salt! I use 1tsp kosher salt in the sauce and I always salt/pepper my chicken before putting it in the crock pot. I use at least 3-4lb's of chicken and pour the sauce over the chicken. There is plenty of sauce. I also put all of the sauce ingredients including half of the onion and half of 1 cup of raisins into a blender to mix it up really well. Cook in the crock pot on low for 5hrs and shred it. I think it tastes better the next day when all the spices are melded together.

This has wonderful flavor. For those who don't like raisins-this recipe really needs them for a layer of fruitiness that gives extra depth to this sauce as well as making it authentic. I used an immersion blender to give it a smooth texture and I didn't notice the raisins but did notice that rich flavor. I didn't have sesame seeds handy and wasn't sure what they would add flavor-wise but just in case, I added a teaspoon of tahini (sesame seed paste). I had some Mexican chocolate on hand so I used that and didn't add any sugar. I also didn't add any chicken but just made a big ol' pot of sauce and cooked the chicken separately. So far I have made mole soft tacos and chicken mole enchiladas and still had enough sauce left over to freeze for a future yummy dish. Thanks for the recipe! It's a keeper! (Oh, and please note-the recipe only calls for ONE chili in adobo sauce, not a whole can. This was just right for me but if you like hot you might want to use 2)

Since this is my first time having chicken mole I went into it with no prejudice or anything to compare it with. Very nice on tortillas, and easy as well. It will be made again. I did lower the level of peanut butter and added some smoked paprika, but otherwise followed the recipe.
Pretty good, you could definitely add more chicken to this amount of sauce.

This is my first time making a mole sauce. I put everything into a blender to mix it up. I don't like raisins but read the reviews that said to NOT leave them out. So, I blended them along with the onions, stewed tomatoes (yes I added an extra small can besides the 28 oz.). I also used both breasts and thighs and shredded them after they were cooked. I plan to make rice tomorrow when we actually eat this. One review said the sauce is better on day 2 so that's what I'm doing~ serving it tomorrow. I have limes & cilantro ready to wash and cut. I also think it seems a bit bitter so I may add the apple cider vinegar that one suggested. Thank you for getting me out of my comfort box!
We loved this and will definitely put on repeat! Phenomenal flavor

Minimal effort and the 'dump and go' aspect of the dish were big selling points. My usual mole takes a half day of hands-on effort and about twelve more ingredients. This was close enough to please everyone and took less than fifteen minutes of prep. I keep a blendered can of chipotle in adobo in the fridge, so I translated 1 chipotle chile in adobo to 1/4 cup of my blended staple. In the future, I will add more chicken (probably double) and mince the raisins beforehand. The appearance of whole raisins in the mole was okay, but slightly unusual for us. It was truly top notch and will be made again.

Made this for dinner last night and WOW this is going to be one of those recipes that gets made over and over again at our house. Delicious, easy to prepare, low in fats, sugars and salt so even my friend who is heart health conscious can enjoy a meal. I served it with rice only because I had forgotten to get radishes, cilantro & limes (three MUSTS at our house for tacos) and there was plenty of extra sauce for the rice to soak up. I followed the recipe exactly, but added more chipotle and Adobo than the recipe called for (I used 1/2 can) because we like things a little spicier here. FANTASTIC!

This was excellent! I used boneless skinless thighs. I omitted the nutmeg and sesame seeds. Very easy to make and the chicken was fall apart tender. You could add a can of rinsed and drained black beans for more protein. I served over baked potatoes.
Needs some lime juice at the end! Overall a very good hands-off recipe. Doesn’t live up to an authentic mole that someone has spent many hours on, but very worthwhile for a weeknight dinner.
This wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t great either. Didn’t taste like any mole I’ve had before. We ate it, but wouldn’t make it again.
